items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: I remember one band that came in from New England named Don Gann.

ctx.x: So what you had then was a lot of bands with local reputations, territory bands I guess they called them.

Oh, far from territory. You mean generally? Before the 30s. Well, the bands I mentioned, like Lopez and Whiteman, of course, were nationally known. Yeah. They were the, Saratoga got the best that could be gotten. It was very wealthy. And it's one month, actually for one month, the month of August, when the racing season was on. Maybe a five week season or so. Sometimes it was. But there were territory bands, of course. New England was loaded with a number of them. And the New York. Western New York, Pennsylvania,…
Yet he came out of Duke, didn't he?
